name: Temporal lift

lead: A temporal lift (temple lift) is a plastic-surgery procedure that elevates the skin and deeper tissue at the temple so the outer end of the eyebrow rises and the skin beside the eye is pulled up and back. The aim is a higher, more lifted lateral brow and a more open look to the eye area.

Surgeons describe it for drooping of the tail of the brow and crow's-feet, and it is often combined with other lifts or an eyelid operation. Published reports are surgeon case series, some with patient-satisfaction questionnaires, rather than randomised trials.

paras: The operation is done by a surgeon through incisions placed in the hair-bearing temple area or just at the hairline, using one of several techniques (subcutaneous, galeapexy, deep temporal, endoscopic). Tissue is lifted and fixed in a higher position. It may be done on its own or alongside eyelid surgery or a cheek-neck lift.

As with other brow and forehead procedures, reported issues include scarring, numbness or tingling, temporary hair thinning near the incision, asymmetry, and, rarely, injury to the facial nerve branch to the forehead. Surgeons describe an over-lifted brow as an undesired outcome, and results can relax over time.

chain: Lifts tissue at temple and outer brow
Tail of brow rises and lateral eye skin tightens
angle.text: The outer eyebrow and the skin beside the eye are physically repositioned upward, which is how people use it to alter eyebrow shape, lateral eye tilt and the look of crow's-feet. It is performed by a surgeon, often combined with other procedures.

lead: A temporal lift, also called a temple lift, is a surgical procedure that raises the tissue of the temple and the lateral (outer) part of the eyebrow. Surgical literature describes it as the treatment for lateral ptosis, or drooping, of the tail of the brow; total brow ptosis is addressed with a frontal lift instead [1]. It overlaps with the lateral brow lift and is classed among the brow-lift approaches [2].

In looksmaxxing forums the temporal lift is discussed as a way to reshape the eye area: members describe the lifted tail of the brow as producing a more positive canthal tilt, tighter under-eye skin and a younger look [3][4]. Surgeons describe related benefits such as improved crow's-feet and a smoother transition between upper and mid-face [5][6].

Research consists of surgeon case series and reviews. Reported series include 270 temporal lifts by galeapexy [7], 212 patients with a modified orbicularis repositioning technique using FACE-Q scores [8] and 250 temporal facelifts [9].

paras: Temporal lifting raises the lateral brow and the temple soft tissue. A French review describes it as belonging to the traditional facelift in its upper part, a junction between the upper and lower face, with indications centred on lateral ptosis of the brow tail; it is often paired with a cervico-cheek lift and can be combined with blepharoplasty [1].

Techniques named in the literature include galeapexy, endoscopic temporal lift, open brow lift with hair-bearing temporal lift, facial threads, an absorbable fixation implant and botulinum toxin [1][3]. A review of the subcutaneous lateral temporal lift describes a technique developed from open coronal and endoscopic approaches that elevates the lateral brow reliably with minimal complications [5].

A series of 270 galeapexy temporal lifts treated the ptotic tail of the brow and crow's feet, with an average patient age of 45 [7]. In the temporal modified orbicularis repositioning series, 212 patients were followed for 12 months with FACE-Q questionnaires and independent surgeon scoring, and no major complications were recorded [8]. A six-year series of 250 temporal facelifts described mid-face elevation, canthopexy and brow lift through a plane above the subgaleal fascia [9].
A systematic review found that combining cervicofacial and temporal lifting with orbicularis muscle procedures was described in 14 studies as a way to improve crow's feet [6].

Reviews of open brow and temporal techniques discuss complications and patient expectations as part of preoperative evaluation [3]. Sensory change, scarring and nerve injury are the issues most associated with lateral brow surgery; anatomical work highlights the temporo-facial branch of the facial nerve and the supraorbital nerve as structures to protect [1].

On looksmax.org, threads call the temple lift an underrated operation that gives 'pct eyes and eyebrows' and reduces signs of ageing [4]. Another thread cautions that a person whose brow already tilts upward could end up over-lifted, and users discuss concerns about scar visibility with short hair [3].

Published studies are retrospective surgeon series and reviews rather than randomised trials. They report maintained brow elevation and high satisfaction with few complications in 212 and 250 patient series [8][9], and a 270-case review of galeapexy [7]. A 2023 ASPS member survey examined how brow-lifting practice patterns changed between 2000 and 2020 [10].
